new.title: Buy royal chocolates at Au Roi Soleil
new.desc: This chocolate and confectionery shop has stood on rue de la Paroisse since 1953, and plays on the tradition begun when Louis XIV brought chocolate to the court of Versailles. Pralines, ganaches and unusual flavours sit beside sugared almonds and a corner of fine tableware.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Saturday, closed for lunch only between 13:00 and 14:00. It is a short walk from the Notre-Dame market, so pair the two.
new.q: Au Roi Soleil, 46 rue de la Paroisse, Versailles

new.title: Pick handmade sweets at Aux Colonnes
new.desc: Aux Colonnes is a former tea room and chocolate shop that has traded at 14 rue Hoche since 1912, run by the Merienne family. Chocolates and confections are made by hand in a workshop open to the shop.
new.tip: Go on a weekday morning for the freshest selection. It is a few minutes from the Notre-Dame market and the Chateau.

new.title: Taste a Meilleur Ouvrier chocolate at Patrick Roger
new.desc: Patrick Roger won the Meilleur Ouvrier de France title in chocolate in 2000 and the World Chocolate Cup in 1994. His Saint-Germain shop on rue de Paris sells sculpted, intensely flavoured bonbons and bars.
new.tip: Buy a small box of pralines to eat on the walk to the Terrace. Rue de Paris is a few minutes from the RER station.
new.q: Patrick Roger Chocolatier, 2 rue de Paris, Saint-Germain-en-Laye

new.title: Try Pascal Le Gac's chocolates on rue de Pologne
new.desc: Pascal Le Gac has run his chocolate shop in Saint-Germain-en-Laye since 2008 and is named among the ten best chocolatiers by the Club des croqueurs de chocolat.
new.tip: Ask for his signature pralines and ganaches. The shop is a short stroll from the chateau and the market.
new.q: Pascal Le Gac Chocolatier, 61 rue de Pologne, Saint-Germain-en-Laye

new.title: Order seafood at the Auberge du Louvetier
new.desc: This Rambouillet restaurant specialises in fish, shellfish and crustaceans, in a calm setting near the forest on the way to the Chevreuse valley. There is a fireplace in the dining room in winter and a covered terrace in warmer months.
new.tip: Open daily for lunch and dinner but with several closed slots (Monday all day), so check the hours and book. Menus start around 28 euros.
new.q: Auberge du Louvetier, 19 rue de l'Etang de la Tour, Rambouillet

new.title: Dine on village classics at the Auberge de l'Elan
new.desc: This village inn at La Celle-les-Bordes sits between the Rambouillet forest and the Chevreuse valley and holds the Maitre Restaurateur label. Its signatures are calf's head and sauteed sweetbreads in a morel sauce, cooked with local, seasonal produce.
new.tip: Open Thursday to Saturday and Sunday lunch only, and booking is required. There is public parking across the street.
new.q: Auberge de l'Elan, 5 rue du Village, La Celle-les-Bordes

new.title: Lunch at the Auberge du Chasseur in Grosrouvre
new.desc: A country house in the centre of Grosrouvre, at the edge of the Rambouillet forest, with a garden and a shaded terrace. It serves traditional and creative cooking from local seasonal products and holds Gault et Millau and Maitre Restaurateur labels.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Saturday for lunch and dinner and Sunday for lunch. Reserve ahead; it also has a wine shop.
new.q: Auberge du Chasseur, 1 route de la Surie, Grosrouvre
